summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology, with a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication. Firmware work centers on bare-metal C for STM32 Cortex-M4: timer-triggered ADC conversions, interrupt-driven capture, and register-level I2C and GPIO drivers, plus FreeRTOS scheduling with mutex-protected shared state. Also fabricated EAGLE PCBs, built closed loop sensor feedback over UART and I2C, and debugged bring-up with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware-software integration.
Organized 10+ technical workshops training junior members on Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth over an HID interface.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver written from the register level up.

projects.name: STM32 Real-Time Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control on STM32 with interrupt-driven UART command parsing and a manual user-override path.
Coordinated concurrent firmware tasks under FreeRTOS using mutex-protected shared state to eliminate race conditions on shared position data.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 hardware-software integration failures including servo brown-out under simultaneous actuation and serial link recovery; achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on an Arduino/AVR microcontroller, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection from dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over an I2C multiplexer.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
